description:
A SECOND task requesting the same refund is denied by the policy duplicate-action guard.
The ACCEPTED_NOT_APPLIED fault is deliberate: it leaves an action row in place while the payment's refundable balance is untouched. Without it the balance check fires first and the duplicate guard is never reached — which is correct defence-in-depth, but leaves the guard untested.
Distinct from REF-22, which is blocked earlier by the approval-state check on a single task.
request: Find the duplicate payment and refund it.

request: Find the duplicate payment and refund it.

description: An accepted-but-unapplied refund is settled by reconciliation, not left PARTIAL forever.
request: Find the duplicate payment and refund it.

description: The refund is accepted, but the verification read-back itself fails. The system cannot see the resulting business state, so it must report UNKNOWN. Reporting SUCCESS here — on the strength of the create response alone — is the false verification the whole design exists to prevent.

description:
The agent requests a tool that is not in the registry. Gate 1 rejects it before argument validation, policy, or anything else runs. There is no dynamic dispatch to fall through to, so an unregistered name has no execution path at all.
Added because a coverage check found this gate had a unit test but no scenario — the deterministic planner can only emit registered tools, so nothing exercised it end to end.

description:
A secret pasted into the user's request must not survive into the audit trail. The raw request is recorded on the task_created event, so this is a real path through redact() — not a hypothetical one.
Added after a coverage check showed redaction had a unit test on the pure function but nothing exercising the end-to-end path.
